gold.title: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiproce
gold.description: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.

candidate.title: Hung flusher processes are never killed — isinstance guard is always false
candidate.description: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is always false for SpawnProcess objects, so process.kill() never executes. On hang paths, processes aren't killed and new ones spawn for the same shards, causing duplicate segment production and accumulation of orphan flushers with Redis connection leaks.

gold.description: Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

candidate.description: time.sleep is patched to a lambda at line 15, so sleep(0.1) at line 62 returns immediately. Comment claims it gives flusher threads time to process, but the monkeypatch defeats this.

promotion_candidates.title: Class docstring claims one process per shard; default is one for all shards
promotion_candidates.description: Docstring says 'Creates one process per shard' but --flusher-processes defaults to 1, making a single process handle all shards. Documentation contradicts the shipped default behavior.
